Vs.
Surendra Chandra Das  and ors ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 8. It is seen from the note of the order Book dated 2-11-92/3-11-93 that defendant appellant opposite party No. 1 Surendra Chandra Das died 2/3 years before as per the service return of the process server dated 24-5-92. This fact of the death of Surendra Das was pointed out by me while delivering judgment on 7-5-97. On such pointing out the learned Counsel for the plaintiff respondent petitioner prayed for time to take step in the matter of substitution of the heirs of deceased Surendra Chandra Das and today the learned Counsel for the plaintiff respondent petitioner has come up with an application under section 151 of Code of Civil Procedure for adding the heir of deceased defendant appellant opposite party No. 1 by deleting his name and adding Anjali Bala Dutta, his daughter, as opposite party No. 1. It is stated in the petition under section 151, Code of Civil Procedure that Surendra Chandra Das died during the pendency of Title Appeal No. 92 of 1984. It is further stated that in the decree prepared in the aforesaid Title Appeal Anjali Bala Dutta, daughter of Surendra Chandra Das was duly substituted in place of her deceased father. It is contended by the learned counsel for the plaintiff respondent petitioner that due to oversight and bona-fide mistake the name of Anjali Bala Dutta was not shown in the cause Title of the revisional application in place of Surendra Chandra Das, the deceased defendant appellant opposite party No. 1. It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the plaintiff respondent petitioner that this mistake being a bonafide mistake can be cured by deleting the name of the defendant appellant opposite party No. 1 Surendra Chandra Das and putting the name of his daughter Anjali Bala Dutta as defendant appellant opposite party No. 1. This court by exercising its inherent power as envisaged in section 151 Code of Civil Procedure can amend the revisional application for the ends of justice. According to him, the proposed amendment can be effected by condoning the delay that occurred under section 143, Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention the learned Counsel for the plaintiff respondent petitioner refers to two decisions reported in 41 DLR 143 and 49 DLR 118. It is argued by the learned counsel for the plaintiff respondent petitioner that in both the cases the heirs of some deceased persons were brought on record in the revisional applications under section 115(1) of Code of Civil Procedure, like the instant case. Likewise Anjali Bala Dutta, daughter of deceased defendant appellant opposite party No. 1 having been substituted in Title Appeal No. 92 of 1984 can be added as defendant appellant opposite party No. 1 in place of her deceased father Surendra Chandra Das. It is argued by the learned Counsel for the plaintiff respondent petitioner that the defendant appellant opposite party No. 2 will not suffer any loss in the event of substitution of the name of Anjali Bala Dutta in place of her deceased father as defendant appellant opposite party No. 2 claims to be in possession of the suit land.
